دَوَلٌ , as an epithet applied to نَبْلٌ [or arrows] i. q. ↓ مُتَدَاوَلٌ . (IAar, M, K. *) So in the saying, “يُلُوذُ بِالجَوْدِ مِنَ النَّبْلِ الدَّوَلْ
” [app. relating to a wild animal, and meaning. He seeks, or takes, refuge in the copious rain from the arrows received in turns by one after another of the herd]. (IAar, M.) ＝
-A2- See also دَوْلَةٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
